definition: Software technology that automates repetitive, rule-based digital tasks by mimicking the actions a human would take within software applications.
details: RPA is often distinguished from more flexible AI agent systems by its reliance on predefined, rule-based scripts rather than adaptive reasoning, though modern platforms increasingly blend RPA with AI capabilities.

explainer.lead: RPA is software that automates repetitive, rule-based digital tasks by mimicking what a human would do inside applications. It matters because it removes routine screen work without redesigning the underlying systems.

tiers.eli5: It is a software robot that clicks and types through computer programs the same way a person would, doing the boring repeated steps for you.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers script predefined rules that replay human actions across applications; modern platforms increasingly blend RPA with AI. A pitfall is expecting adaptive reasoning from rule-based scripts.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as rule-based automation of repetitive digital tasks via predefined scripts mimicking human actions, distinguished from adaptive AI agents. Its limit is brittleness outside the rules it was scripted for.

explainer.example: A script opens an invoice email, copies the amount into a finance application and files the record, repeating it for every message.
